card.title: First to Solve It
card.instruction: Treat each clue and inconsistency as a contest over who can understand the situation first and most completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've solved your missing parcel. Tracking says reception; you were still refreshing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for three boxes. Only two reached our office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one stayed downstairs. I've narrowed your whole building to one desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The trolley's here. There's a box wedged underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it left reception but never got unloaded. You've found the parcel; I've solved why we've been calling reception all morning.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims to solve the parcel before B, A3 claims superior narrowing after the box discrepancy, and A5 competes on explaining the cause after B finds the object.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's three-versus-two count informs A3's downstairs theory; B4's wedged box forces A5 to claim causal understanding instead of discovery.

relationship.evidence: B2 provides actual tracking-receipt detail and B4 physically locates the missing box.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's decisive discovery to shift the contest from finding where to explaining why.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish an office parcel delivered through reception, with one box missing upstairs.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's you-found-I-solved distinction follows B4's success rather than ignoring it.

coach2.situation: A1-B2 establish an office parcel delivered through reception, with one box missing upstairs.
coach2.stated: B4 explicitly corrects A3's theory; A5 updates it, so the wrong intermediate inference is not a continuity failure.
coach2.inferred: A1-B4 establish coworkers tracing a missing delivery.
coach2.missing: No essential gap; the trolley explains how a delivered box can remain unnoticed.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; each clue changes which part of understanding A claims to win.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 complicates A1's reception solution with the box count.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 contradicts A3's downstairs assumption by finding the box on the trolley.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 accepts B4's location and claims superiority in explaining the unloading failure.
